svg.title: Hazardous materials control zones
svg.desc: Three nested control zones drawn as rectangles, with the wind blowing from the left. Innermost is the HOT ZONE, the exclusion zone containing the release: only trained personnel in appropriate protection enter, and the only patient care is getting the patient out - no assessment, no treatment, no vital signs. Around it is the WARM ZONE, the decontamination corridor, where contamination is reduced and protective equipment is removed in sequence; life-saving intervention only, by trained and protected people. Outermost is the COLD ZONE, containing the command post, staging, the treatment area, transport and the ambulances, and this is where EMTs work; nothing contaminated enters it. A single one-way arrow runs from hot through warm into cold, labelled ONE WAY ONLY, with a note that reverse movement requires going through the whole process again. A wind arrow at the top left is labelled: position upwind and uphill, and if the wind shifts the zones move - including wherever you parked.
svg.text: HAZMAT CONTROL ZONES
Hot, warm, cold — and movement runs one way only.
WIND
Position UPWIND and UPHILL. If the wind shifts, THE ZONES MOVE — including where you parked.
COLD ZONE — support
Command post · staging · TREATMENT · transport · the ambulances
THIS IS WHERE EMTs WORK, unless specifically trained and equipped otherwise
NOTHING CONTAMINATED ENTERS — not a patient, not a responder, not a piece of kit
WARM ZONE — decontamination corridor
Contamination is REDUCED on the way out · PPE removed IN SEQUENCE
Trained, protected decontamination personnel only
LIFE-SAVING INTERVENTION ONLY — not general patient care
HOT ZONE — exclusion
Contains the release. Everything inside is contaminated
Trained personnel in appropriate protection ONLY
NO PATIENT CARE BEYOND GETTING THEM OUT
No assessment. No treatment. No vital signs.
ONE WAY ONLY
HOT → WARM → COLD. Never back without going
through the whole process again.
Every shortcut across a boundary makes the incident bigger — and shortcuts are always taken by well-meaning people in a hurry.
CONTAMINATED PATIENTS NEVER ENTER THE AMBULANCE. An interior cannot be decontaminated, and a contaminated vehicle is
out of service and a hazard in itself.
Zone definitions, entry criteria and your own scope in each zone are set by your local protocol and hazmat plan. Confirm before use.
